Definition: from G5259 and G5087; to place underneath, i.e. (figuratively) to hazard, (reflexively) to suggest:--lay down, put in remembrance.
BiblicalUsage: hypotíthēmi means to lay down, to put in remembrance. In Romans 16:4, the text says "Who have for my life laid down their own necks."
TheologicalSignificance: This word, hypotíthēmi, does its job quietly — to lay down, to put in remembrance — and I leave it at that.
